p.src: Entanglement belongs at the heart of quantum mechanics, but the foundations are now sufficiently exposed that we can begin using them. The course has so far relied on deliberately small systems: a spin, a rotatable apparatus, a finite list of outcomes, and repeated measurements from which probabilities are inferred. Those experiments are logically simpler than the historical path by which quantum mechanics was discovered, but they contain the minimum operational ingredients.

A broad class of sufficiently regular functions can be decomposed into such modes. We restrict attention to functions that behave well enough for the integrals below: they are not allowed to blow up at spatial infinity, and later physical wave functions will be square-integrable. With a symmetric normalization convention, the Fourier pair is $\begin{aligned}\psi(x)
&=
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
\frac{dp}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,
\widetilde{\psi}(p)e^{ipx},
\\
\widetilde{\psi}(p)
&=
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
\frac{dx}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,
\psi(x)e^{-ipx}.
\end{aligned}$ The coefficient $\widetilde{\psi}(p)$ is the complex amplitude of the mode with Fourier label $p$. The factors of $1/\sqrt{2\pi}$ are conventional; placing one in each direction makes the two formulas look reciprocal. The relative minus sign in the exponent is essential.

p.src:
The intuitive delta function is a spike of vanishing width, diverging height, and unit area. That picture is useful, but the operational definition is more reliable. For every suitable test function $f$, $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
dx\,\delta(x-x')f(x)
=f(x').$ Three familiar rules express the same idea: $\begin{aligned}f(x)\delta(x-x')
&=
f(x')\delta(x-x'),
\\
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dx\,\delta(x-x')
&=1,
\\
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dx\,\delta(x-x')f(x)
&=f(x').\end{aligned}$ The first rule holds because the delta has support only where $x=x'$. In the second rule, translating the spike changes its location but not its area. Combining those two rules gives the third.

p.src: The mathematical interlude was not separate from the physics. Plane waves and the Dirac delta built the continuous basis machinery. The position operator acts by multiplication, the momentum operator acts by differentiation, and momentum eigenstates are plane waves. Projecting an arbitrary state onto those eigenstates produces the Fourier transform of its position wave function. Position and momentum are therefore rival representations of one state, and their uncertainty is the familiar reciprocal width of a Fourier pair.

ja: 数学的間奏は物理学から切り離されたものではなかった。平面波とディラックのデルタが連続基底の仕組みを構築した。位置演算子は掛け算として作用し、運動量演算子は微分として作用し、運動量固有状態は平面波である。任意の状態をそれらの固有状態に射影すると、その位置波動関数のフーリエ変換が得られる。したがって位置と運動量は一つの状態の競合する表現であり、それらの不確定性はフーリエ対のよく知られた逆幅の関係である。
zh: 这段数学插曲并非与物理分离。平面波和狄拉克 δ 构建了连续基的机制。位置算符通过乘法作用，动量算符通过微分作用，动量本征态是平面波。将任意态投影到这些本征态上，就得到其位置波函数的傅里叶变换。因此，位置和动量是同一个态的两种相互竞争的表象，它们的不确定性就是傅里叶对之间熟悉的倒数宽度关系。

u.src: The same representation machinery then turns a Hamiltonian into a differential equation. A linear function of momentum produces rigid translation; the quadratic kinetic energy produces the free-particle Schrödinger equation and dispersion. The course has moved from the foundations of measurement to the mechanics of motion without changing its central language: states, bases, Hermitian observables, amplitudes, and unitary evolution.
en: The same representation machinery then turns a Hamiltonian into a differential equation. A linear function of momentum produces rigid translation; the quadratic kinetic energy produces the free-particle Schrödinger equation and dispersion. The course has moved from the foundations of measurement to the mechanics of motion without changing its central language: states, bases, Hermitian observables, amplitudes, and unitary evolution.
ja: 同じ表現の仕組みが、次にハミルトニアンを微分方程式に変える。運動量の線形関数は剛体的平行移動を生み出し、二次の運動エネルギーは自由粒子 Schrödinger 方程式と分散を生み出す。この講義は、測定の基礎から運動の力学へと、その中心的な言語を変えることなく移行した。すなわち状態、基底、エルミート演算子、振幅、そしてユニタリ発展である。
zh: 随后，同一套表象机制把哈密顿量变成微分方程。动量的线性函数产生刚性平移；二次型动能产生自由粒子 Schrödinger 方程和色散。本课程已从测量基础推进到运动力学，而其核心语言始终未变：态、基、厄米可观测量、振幅和幺正演化。
